en.title: Fast Phrases and Weak Forms
en.summary: Learn how to link words smoothly and pronounce weak forms naturally at normal speaking speed.

sections.title: The sound
paragraphs: People speak fast in daily life. Small words lose their full strength. They join bigger words to make one smooth flow. Listen to (n-am timp) /nam tʲimp/, which means I do not have time. The little negative word links right to the verb. The weak word has no heavy stress.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: Relax your mouth and jaw. Do not pause between the small words. Say (n-am timp) /nam tʲimp/ in a single breath. Place the main beat on the last word. Keep your tongue light on the first sound. Let the sounds flow together like one long word.

sections.title: Reading rules
paragraphs: A hyphen often shows a weak form in writing. The hyphen drops a vowel and joins two words. Look at the phrase (n-am timp) /nam tʲimp/. Here, (nu) /nu/ loses a vowel and joins (am) /am/. Read hyphenated pairs without stopping. Treat them as a single spoken unit.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not stress every single word equally. Do not stop at the hyphen. Some learners say each piece slowly and separate the sounds. This sounds stiff and robotic. Keep the first part soft and fast. Push the main energy toward the end of the phrase.
